tagline: Along the ridge, with river valleys below.
intro: From Marianna the St. Francis Scenic Byway follows the crest of Crowley’s Ridge toward Helena-West Helena, with views into the Mississippi and St. Francis river valleys. Bear Creek Lake and Storm Creek Lake lie along the way. Between the lakes, much of the road is gravel.
Marianna began as Walnut Ridge, a name it gave up in 1852. Cotton production long supported the town beside the L’Anguille River; the byway leaves that river town for the crest of the ridge.

moments.title: Marianna
moments.text: Marianna stands beside the L’Anguille River, where a break in Crowley’s Ridge leaves room for a town whose fortunes long depended on cotton.

moments.title: Bear Creek Lake
moments.text: Bear Creek Lake, the larger of the two at 625 acres, marks one end of the gravel on Forest Service Road 1900.

moments.title: Storm Creek Lake
moments.text: Storm Creek Lake, 420 acres, waits at the other end of about fourteen miles of gravel along the ridge.

practical: About fourteen miles of Forest Service Road 1900 remain gravel between Bear Creek Lake and Storm Creek Lake recreation areas.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, St. Francis Scenic Byway
